summary: This resolution sets House floor procedures for debating and voting on two Senate joint resolutions to disapprove an OCC rule on bank merger reviews and an EPA rule on Clean Air Act source reclassifications, while waiving the two-thirds vote requirement for same-day consideration of Rules Committee reports on reconciliation measures through May 23, 2025.

scores.thoughts: The resolution includes a procedural waiver (section 3) allowing same-day consideration of rules committee reports related to reconciliation measures under H. Con. Res. 14. Reconciliation is a budget process that can affect government spending levels. However, the bill itself is purely procedural and does not direct any specific spending changes, so any connection is indirect and minor.

Section 3 references reconciliation procedures, which can be used for tax legislation. The bill does not enact or direct any tax policy changes and remains a rules package, resulting in only a tangential link.
No provisions in the bill address healthcare policy, coverage, or regulation.
No provisions relate to firearms, regulations, or rights.
No provisions address immigration, borders, or related protections.
No provisions address abortion access or restrictions.
No provisions address military or defense spending or policy.

Section 2 sets up expedited consideration of S.J. Res. 31, which would disapprove an EPA rule under the Clean Air Act concerning reclassification of major sources as area sources. Disapproval would limit environmental regulation, creating a direct (though procedural) engagement with the topic.
No provisions address welfare programs, food assistance, or related benefits.
No provisions address schools, funding, or education policy.
No provisions address drug enforcement, decriminalization, or related rules.
No provisions address sentencing, policing, or justice reform.
No provisions address trade, tariffs, or globalization.
Section 3 references reconciliation, a process often used in debt and deficit management. The connection is indirect and procedural only.
No provisions address LGBTQ+ legal protections or related civil rights.
No provisions address foreign aid or international assistance.
No provisions address voting access, election integrity, or related reforms.
No provisions address technology regulation, data privacy, or oversight.
No provisions address worker protections, unions, or employer flexibility.
No provisions address religious exemptions or anti-discrimination rules.
